title: Part 67 & 68: Medical Standards
description: Medical certificate classes, requirements, durations, BasicMed, and fitness for flight

cards.back:
First Class: Required for ATP privileges
Second Class: Required for commercial privileges
Third Class: Required for private/recreational/student

Higher class = more stringent requirements

Under 40: 12 calendar months (first class privileges)
Age 40+: 6 calendar months (first class privileges)

After expiration of first class privileges, continues as second class, then third class

All ages: 12 calendar months (second class privileges)

After expiration of second class privileges, continues as third class

Under 40: 60 calendar months (5 years)
Age 40+: 24 calendar months (2 years)

Memory aid: 'Under 40 = 5 years, Over 40 = 2 years'

Expires at the END of the month shown

Example: Certificate dated March 15, 2024 expires March 31, 2024 (for that class privilege)

Distant: 20/40 or better each eye (with or without correction)
Near: 20/40 or better at 16 inches (with or without correction)
Intermediate: 20/40 at 32 inches if age 50+ (with or without correction)

Correctve lenses must be worn if required

Distant: 20/20 or better each eye (with or without correction)
Near: 20/40 or better at 16 inches
Intermediate: 20/40 at 32 inches

More stringent than third class!

Must perceive colors necessary for safe performance of airman duties

If failed: Limitation placed on certificate
• 'Not valid for night flying'
• 'Not valid for color signal control'

Alternative tests available (OCVT, MFT)

Demonstrate hearing of average conversational voice at 6 feet
• Quiet room
• Back turned to examiner

OR pass audiometric test

To use BasicMed:
1. Valid driver's license
2. Held medical after July 15, 2006
3. Physical exam every 48 months
4. Online course every 24 months
5. No denial/revocation of most recent medical

Carry: Checklist, course completion, driver's license

Aircraft: ≤6 seats, ≤6000 lbs MTOW
Altitude: Below 18,000' MSL
Speed: ≤250 KIAS
Passengers: ≤5 (6 seats minus pilot)
Operations: No compensation/hire

Memory aid: '6-6-18-250'

Cannot use BasicMed if:
• Most recent medical denied/suspended/revoked
• Never held medical after July 15, 2006
• Certain mental health conditions
• Cardiac conditions requiring special issuance

Must obtain regular medical first to 'reset'

No person may act as PIC or required crewmember:
• Knowing of medical condition that would prevent meeting medical standards
• While taking medication that affects ability to operate safely

Applies even with valid medical certificate!

I - Illness (Am I sick?)
M - Medication (Taking any?)
S - Stress (Under pressure?)
A - Alcohol (8 hours, 0.04%?)
F - Fatigue (Adequate rest?)
E - Emotion (Emotionally fit?)

Use before EVERY flight!

Physician designated by FAA to conduct medical exams

Find AME: medxpress.faa.gov

MedXpress: Online application system (complete before exam)

Medical certificate issued to pilots who don't meet standard requirements

Requires:
• Documentation of condition
• Demonstration of safe operation
• Often requires periodic testing
• May have limitations

Examples:
• Diabetes requiring medication
• Heart conditions
• Certain mental health conditions
• Substance dependence history
• Neurological conditions

Not automatic denial-SI process available

8 hours bottle to throttle
0.04% BAC maximum
No impairment from alcohol

2 alcohol-related motor vehicle convictions in 3 years = grounds for denial

Must report DUI within 60 days

Many medications are disqualifying:
• Sedatives
• Certain antihistamines
• Some blood pressure meds
• Antidepressants (some allowed with SI)

Check with AME BEFORE taking new medication

Student pilot certificate: No medical required to obtain

To SOLO: Must have at least third class medical (or BasicMed)

Student certificate no longer expires

Sport pilots may use valid driver's license instead of medical IF:
• Never had medical denied/revoked/suspended
• No known medical condition that makes operation unsafe

Sport pilot limitations apply

No medical certificate required for:
• Glider pilots
• Balloon pilots

Still must self-certify fitness (61.53)
Still subject to 91.17 (alcohol)

Higher class medical 'downgrades' over time:

First class → Second class → Third class

Example: First class at age 42:
• First class: 6 months
• Second class: 6 more months (12 total)
• Third class: 12 more months (24 total)

No requirement to report changes between exams UNLESS:
• Applying for new medical
• Condition makes you unable to meet standards (61.53)

Best practice: Consult AME if uncertain

Disqualifying conditions (may get SI):
• Psychosis
• Bipolar disorder
• Severe personality disorder
• Substance dependence

Depression/anxiety: Many pilots fly with SI after evaluation

First class: ECG required at age 35, then annually at 40+

Disqualifying (may get SI):
• Myocardial infarction
• Coronary artery disease
• Certain arrhythmias
• Heart valve replacement

Disqualifying (may get SI):
• Epilepsy
• Disturbance of consciousness without explanation
• Transient loss of nervous system function

Single seizure: Usually 4-year wait for SI consideration

Maximum (sitting): 155/95

Higher readings: May still qualify if controlled

Medications: Some allowed, some not-check with AME

Diet/exercise controlled: Usually no issue

Oral medications: Special Issuance available

Insulin-dependent: Special Issuance available since 2019 (strict requirements)

Regular Medical:
• Medical certificate

BasicMed:
• Driver's license
• Completed medical exam checklist
• Course completion certificate

Always have photo ID
